arguments: {"test_id": "T1", "per_hypothesis": [{"id": "H1", "verdict": "supported", "why": "Residue 28 lies within 4.5 \u00c5 of an organic ligand in 32 of 39 ligand-bound structures that observe it. The inositol-phosphate ligand 4IP (Ins(1,3,4,5)P4, the ligand named in H1) contacts it in 4 of 6 instances, closest 2.75 \u00c5 (PDB 1BWN). The phosphate-rich 4PT in 2Z0P contacts it at 2.58 \u00c5. Negative-control ligands (ZN, MG, 3IS, 72V, etc.) never contact residue 28. The refutation criterion (no ligand atom within about 4 \u00c5 in Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 or PIP3-type complexes) was not met. Caveat: the contacts are with wild-type R28, not R28H, and most contacting ligands are synthetic benzofuran compounds (A1B6 family), which are not headgroup analogues."}, {"id": "H2", "verdict": "unchanged", "why": "T1 measured ligand proximity only. It did not measure any PH-TH partner-chain contact or dimer interface, so it does not bear on H2."}, {"id": "H3", "verdict": "unchanged", "why": "T1 measured ligand proximity, not folding stability or side-chain burial. It does not bear on H3. The 39 structures with residue 28 were not used to test solvent accessibility either."}], "uncertainty": "T1 completed (executed, verdict contact_with_organic_ligand). Its controls behaved as expected: negative-control ligands never contacted residue 28, and the four R28C-mutant structures had zero ligand contacts. The R28C result cannot be read as R28H evidence, because the mutant removes the side chain in a different way and no R28H structure exists in the set. Contact distance in crystal structures is not binding affinity. Most contacting ligands are soluble synthetic analogues, so the 4IP and 4PT contacts are the only headgroup-relevant data. Validation still needed: a R28H-specific binding free energy against Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 (see next experiment). H1 is supported, not proven; its refutation threshold (about 0.5 kcal/mol) has not yet been tested for R28H."}
